## System prompt (nguyên văn)

```
You are a hostile staff SRE reviewing a change to a live product run by one person. Your job is to find the specific failure this change causes in production. Be concrete: name the mechanism, the trigger, the user-visible symptom. Reject generic risk language. If the change is genuinely safe, say so plainly and briefly.
```

## User prompt / brief (nguyên văn)

````markdown
# Change under review — ThePickleHub (solo-operated, ~2k users, 86% Vietnam traffic)

## System facts (verified in repo; you cannot see the repo, trust these)

- React 18 + Vite SPA on Cloudflare Pages. Bot traffic is server-rendered by a
  Cloudflare Pages Function `functions/_middleware.ts` which detects crawler UA,
  renders HTML, and caches it in Workers KV under key `pr:v32:${pathname}`,
  TTL 6 hours. Query string is NOT part of the cache key. `?nocache=1` bypasses.
  Cache-key version is bumped manually to invalidate everything at once.
- Prerender has an 8s budget; on timeout the bot falls through to the raw SPA
  shell (200, generic title, no body).
- EN blog posts are TypeScript files: `src/content/blog/posts/<slug>.ts` plus an
  entry in `src/content/blog/metadata.ts`. The SSR title table and the sitemap
  slug list are GENERATED from metadata.ts at module load, and two vitest suites
  fail CI on drift. A static barrel `posts/all.ts` (lazy `import()` map) is
  regenerated by a script; a test fails if it drifts.
- VI blog posts are NOT in the repo. They are rows in Supabase table
  `vi_blog_posts` (columns include slug, title, meta_title, meta_description,
  content_html, alternate_en_slug, status). Written via the Supabase Management
  API. There is no migration file and no exported SQL for recent VI posts —
  `growth-tasks/sql/` contains only two files from 2026-05-05.
- Reciprocal hreflang is computed at render time: the EN page queries
  `vi_blog_posts WHERE alternate_en_slug = <en slug>`; the VI page reads its own
  `alternate_en_slug`. If either is missing, that page emits no cross-language
  hreflang.
- The blog content model is `BlogSection { heading, content, listItems?,
  orderedList?, image?, internalLinks? }`. Both renderers escape `content` and
  emit `<p>{escaped}</p>`. `internalLinks` renders as `href="${siteUrl}${path}"`
  — concatenation, so an absolute external URL produces a broken href.
  There is NO field for an external link. Adding one touches the type, the
  React page, and the SSR renderer.
- Headings render as `<h2>{heading}</h2>` in BOTH renderers, with NO `id`
  attribute. There is no anchor mechanism for EN posts.
- VI posts render via `DOMPurify.sanitize(content_html)` in React. Experiment
  confirmed: DOMPurify keeps `id` and `rel`, and STRIPS `target`.
- Content Security Policy (`public/_headers`, mirrored in `_middleware.ts`,
  locked by a parity test): `frame-src` allowlist does not include ticketbox.vn.
  `default-src 'self'`. Plain `<a href>` navigation is unaffected by CSP.
- Homepage `/` renders a "top 6 stories" strip by sorting all blog metadata by
  `publishedDate` descending and slicing 6. It is client-computed and the
  metadata array is in the first-paint entry chunk.
- Bundle gates (CI, `scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs`), measured today:
  INITIAL 267.4 KB gz / budget 280; CODE 1490.7 / 1800; CONTENT (blog chunks)
  357.9 KB across 47 chunks with a 20 KB per-chunk cap; total 1848.6 / 1970.
  Largest existing blog chunk is 15.0 KB gz from 46.6 KB of source.
- A CI test enforces SERP byte budgets on metadata: meta titles ≤ 60 UTF-8
  BYTES, descriptions ≤ 160 BYTES. Vietnamese diacritics cost 2–3 bytes each.
  Another test asserts the post file's SEO strings equal metadata.ts's.
- IndexNow pinging goes through a Pages Function whose "submit everything"
  path uses a HAND-MAINTAINED array of EN blog slugs. It has already drifted:
  46 slugs in metadata.ts, 42 in that array, 4 published posts missing. No test
  covers it.
- The work order's Definition of Done requires updating a file
  `.gsc-index-queue.json`. That file does not exist anywhere in the repo.

## What is proposed

**Task 4 (timely event).** The MB Ho Chi Minh City Open runs 6–9 August 2026;
today is 27 July. An existing EN+VI post `hcmc-open-2026-preview` already covers
it (dates, venue, US$70,000 purse, prize breakdown, FAQ). Proposal:
  (a) add internal links to it from a top-performing VI post, a calendar post,
      the homepage, and `/live`;
  (b) publish a NEW companion "how to watch / buy tickets" post, EN + VI, that
      links out to the official ticket page `https://ticketbox.vn/ppa-asia-500-mb-hcmc-open-2026-26355`
      (verified live today, HTTP 200; its embedded JSON confirms
      startDate 2026-08-06, endDate 2026-08-09, venue "New Sports Club, City
      Park, The Global City"; no ticket price is present in server HTML);
  (c) refresh `updatedDate` on the existing preview and re-ping IndexNow.

Note: the existing preview post's prose contains time-bound sentences written on
23 July and now stale — it says a rival tournament (Singapore Open, 23–26 July)
is "under way now" / "this week", and says the pro line-up is unannounced "as of
July 23, just over two weeks out". It also names the venue "Global City Sports
Park", while the ticket seller calls it "New Sports Club, City Park, The Global
City".

**Task 5 (glossary pillar).** Publish a Vietnamese glossary
`/vi/blog/thuat-ngu-pickleball` (Supabase row) with one anchored section per
term (`#kitchen`, `#dink`, `#erne`, …), optionally an EN twin
`/blog/pickleball-glossary` (repo files) for hreflang. Anchors on the EN side
would require adding `id={slugify(heading)}` to the shared heading renderers —
which changes the HTML output of ALL 47 existing EN posts and therefore forces a
`pr:v32 → v33` cache-key bump that discards the entire prerender cache for every
route on the site. Across all 47 existing posts, slugifying every heading
produces exactly one duplicate id, in one post.

The site already ranks for the term "kitchen" via an existing post
`pickleball-rules-complete-guide`, which contains a heading "The Kitchen
(Non-Volley Zone)". The operator has no programmatic Search Console access, so
current ranking positions cannot be measured from the repo.

## Your job

Name the specific production failures these two changes cause: the mechanism,
the trigger, and what a real user or Googlebot sees. Rank them. Say plainly if
some part is safe. Reject anything you cannot ground in the facts above.
Pay attention to ordering/timing hazards, rollback asymmetry between repo
content and database content, and anything that silently produces a
worse-than-before state that nobody would notice for weeks.
````

## Trả lời GPT-5.6 (NGUYÊN VĂN, chưa biên tập)

## Ranked production failures

### 1. Refreshing the preview’s `updatedDate` without refreshing its prose publishes a falsely current article

**Mechanism:** The change advertises a fresh update while retaining statements tied to 23 July.

**Trigger:** Task 4(c) changes `updatedDate`, and the new homepage/calendar/live links send more traffic to the preview.

**What users and Googlebot see:**

- A newly updated article saying the 23–26 July Singapore Open is “under way now” or happening “this week,” although it ended on 26 July.
- “As of July 23, just over two weeks out,” even though it is now 27 July.
- An unresolved venue discrepancy: “Global City Sports Park” versus the ticket seller’s “New Sports Club, City Park, The Global City.”

This is worse than leaving the old timestamp alone: the site explicitly vouches that stale information was recently checked. Fix the prose and reconcile the venue before touching `updatedDate`.

---

### 2. The EN ticket link is broken unless the content model and both renderers change together

The existing EN model cannot represent an external link correctly.

#### If the ticket URL is put in `internalLinks`

**Mechanism:** The renderer concatenates `siteUrl + path`.

**Trigger:** Supplying  
`https://ticketbox.vn/ppa-asia-500-mb-hcmc-open-2026-26355`  
as an internal-link path.

**User-visible result:** A malformed URL such as:

```text
https://thepicklehub.examplehttps://ticketbox.vn/ppa-asia-500-mb-hcmc-open-2026-26355
```

Clicking “Buy tickets” does not reach Ticketbox.

#### If it is put in `content`

**Mechanism:** `content` is escaped and wrapped in `<p>`.

**Result:** Users and Googlebot see plain text or escaped markup, not a crawlable link.

#### If only the React renderer is updated

**Mechanism:** Humans receive the client-rendered link, but crawler SSR still uses the old renderer.

**Result:** Users can click Ticketbox, while Googlebot’s prerendered HTML contains no valid outbound ticket link.

The correct implementation is an explicit external-link field supported by the type, React renderer, and SSR renderer in the same deployment. A plain `<a href>` is allowed by CSP. Do not iframe Ticketbox: `frame-src` blocks it.

For VI, a normal `<a href>` in `content_html` works. `target="_blank"` will be stripped, so it opens in the same tab; that is not a broken link.

---

### 3. Publishing EN and VI separately creates non-reciprocal hreflang, then KV preserves it for six hours

#### EN deployed first

**Mechanism:** The EN prerender queries Supabase before the VI row exists, emits no cross-language hreflang, and stores that HTML in KV.

**Trigger:** Googlebot requests the EN URL after the repo deployment but before the VI insert.

**What Googlebot sees:**

1. EN page with no VI alternate.
2. That result remains cached for up to six hours even after VI is published.
3. VI can meanwhile point back to EN, producing a one-sided pair that Google may ignore.

#### VI published first

**Mechanism:** The VI row immediately names an EN alternate that has not been deployed.

**Trigger:** Googlebot or a user follows the VI page’s EN alternate during the deployment gap.

**Result:** The VI page advertises a not-yet-existing EN companion. The exact missing-route UI is not specified, but the referenced article is absent.

Deploying the two artifacts “close together” does not remove this race because an unlucky bot request can freeze the EN result for six hours. Publish in a controlled order and explicitly bypass/warm both paths with `?nocache=1` after both sides exist.

---

### 4. A repository rollback does not roll back the VI publication

**Mechanism:** EN is versioned in the repository; VI is an unversioned Supabase mutation with no current SQL export or migration.

**Trigger:** The Cloudflare deployment is rolled back after publishing the VI companion or glossary.

**What remains in production:**

- The VI article stays live.
- Its `alternate_en_slug` can point to an EN article removed by the rollback.
- Googlebot sees a dangling hreflang relationship.
- Users following the EN-language alternative reach a route whose article was rolled back.
- Reconstructing the exact previous VI row is manual because the current database changes are not represented in the repository.

This also applies to edits made to the existing top-performing VI post. Capture the previous rows and prepare explicit insert/update/delete rollback SQL before mutating Supabase.

---

### 5. “Submit everything” silently omits the new EN article unless another manual list is updated

**Mechanism:** IndexNow does not use the generated metadata or sitemap slug list. Its bulk path uses a separate hand-maintained array.

**Trigger:** The operator adds the new article to `metadata.ts` and runs “submit everything” without also adding its slug to that array.

**Result:**

- IndexNow never receives the new companion URL.
- The existing four omitted posts remain omitted.
- The command can report success because the submitted subset was accepted.
- There is no test to reveal the omission, so this can remain unnoticed until someone observes delayed discovery or audits the arrays weeks later.

Whether the existing preview itself is among the 42 entries is not given, so I cannot claim its re-ping fails. The new slug, however, necessarily starts absent from the current hand-maintained array.

`.gsc-index-queue.json` is a separate process failure: the Definition of Done requires updating a nonexistent file. It causes no runtime symptom by itself, but the task cannot truthfully be marked complete without first defining and adding that artifact.

---

### 6. Global EN heading IDs introduce one deterministic ambiguous fragment

**Mechanism:** Applying `id={slugify(heading)}` to all shared heading renderers creates duplicate IDs in one existing post.

**Trigger:** A user, search result, or external site opens that post using the duplicated fragment.

**User-visible result:** The browser resolves the fragment to one of the duplicate elements—normally the first in document order—so the user can land on the wrong section.

This is not hypothetical duplicate-ID risk: the supplied corpus check says exactly one collision exists. Resolve collisions deterministically, for example with stable suffixes, before rollout.

The cache-key bump itself definitely makes every crawler route a cold miss. It does **not**, from the supplied facts, definitely cause an outage: there is no evidence those renders exceed eight seconds or that crawler concurrency will overload the renderer. If a render does exceed eight seconds during this cold period, that bot receives the raw 200 SPA shell with a generic title and no body, but claiming that it will happen would be unsupported.

## Safe parts

- A VI-only glossary with sanitized heading `id` attributes is safe: DOMPurify preserves `id`, so `#kitchen`, `#dink`, and similar fragments work.
- Omitting the optional EN glossary twin is not a failure. It simply means there is no cross-language hreflang for that glossary.
- Plain outbound Ticketbox navigation is unaffected by CSP.
- Internal links to the existing preview are safe if they use normal internal paths.
- The new post naturally enters the homepage’s top-six strip through `publishedDate`; refreshing only `updatedDate` does not reorder that strip.
- Ranking cannibalization between the glossary and the existing “kitchen” article cannot be established from these facts. Do not present it as a production failure.
- Bundle-size and UTF-8 SERP-limit violations would fail CI rather than silently reach production. The supplied information does not establish that either limit will be exceeded.
